headline: BHP WINS $14.7B ESCONDIDA GREEN LIGHT — WORLD'S BIGGEST COPPER MINE TO DOUBLE OUTPUT BY 2035 AMID DEFICIT
snippet: Chile's Antofagasta Environmental Assessment Commission approved the first $1.3 billion tranche of BHP's Escondida expansion on July 7 — sulfide leaching upgrades and new electricity infrastructure — unlocking a decade-long, $14.7 billion programme that targets near-doubling of BHP's global copper output to more than two million tonnes annually by the mid-2030s. At a time when Hormuz supply disruptions and elevated shipping costs are reshaping copper supply chains, greenlighting the world's largest copper mine's expansion plan sends a clear signal that major producers are betting the structural copper deficit will sustain prices through the 2030s despite near-term macro headwinds.

headline: K92 KAINANTU RECORD Q2: 46,093 OZ AUEQ, RECORD LATERAL DEVELOPMENT — PNG GOLD MINER ON GUIDANCE TRACK (TSX:KNI)
snippet: K92 Mining (TSX: KNI) reported July 8 that the Kainantu Gold Mine in Papua New Guinea produced 46,093 oz AuEq in Q2 2026, with record quarterly lateral development and record ore tonnes mined and processed — three operating metrics simultaneously at all-time highs in the same quarter, signalling the expansion ramp is running ahead of schedule. For investors comparing operating leverage in the current $4,000+ gold price environment, Kainantu's simultaneous records on mine development, ore handling, and processing efficiency is the type of data that narrows the gap between resource potential and production reality.

headline: CHILE LITHIUM EXPORTS NEARLY TRIPLE TO $3.2B IN H1 — BEST HALF SINCE 2023 AS EV AND AI DEMAND ABSORBS SUPPLY
snippet: Chile's central bank confirmed July 8 that lithium export revenue reached $3.2 billion in H1 2026 — nearly triple the pace of H1 2025 and 34% above Chile's total 2025 exports in just six months, the strongest first half since 2023's boom cycle. The acceleration is demand-driven: EV manufacturers, grid storage operators, AI data centre operators, and semiconductor manufacturers have all been absorbing supply that last year sat in surplus, and Chile's two-producer market is the clearest early read on whether the lithium price recovery has structural depth.

headline: TREATY CREEK SILVER BRECCIA: 7.2M AT 201.84 G/T AG OPENS NEW CBS ZONE DIMENSION IN GOLDEN TRIANGLE (TSX:TUD)
source_name: Globe and Mail / Tudor Gold Corp.
snippet: Tudor Gold (TSX: TUD) reported July 7 that hole CBS-26-08 at Treaty Creek's CBS Zone in BC's Golden Triangle intercepted a new silver-rich breccia corridor returning 34.15m at 61.28 g/t Ag including a 7.20m interval at 201.84 g/t Ag — a high-sulfidation breccia system interpreted as a major fluid-flow corridor within the same geological architecture as Treaty Creek's existing massive gold resource. Companion hole CBS-26-09 extended the mineralised zone 60m vertically up-dip at 47m of 0.79 g/t Au, with two drill rigs returning to the CBS Zone in September after the summer Perfectstorm program completes.

headline: MIATA PUMA DISCOVERY: 17.19M AT 3.14 G/T AU 3KM FROM MAIN CORRIDOR — NEW ZONE AT SELA CREEK, SURINAME (TSXV:MMET)
snippet: Miata Metals Corp. (TSXV: MMET) reported July 7 a significant new gold discovery at the Puma target — approximately 3 kilometres southeast of the Jons Trend–Big Berg Corridor — at the Sela Creek Gold Project in Suriname, with initial holes returning 17.19m at 3.14 g/t Au and 21.64m at 1.70 g/t Au. The Puma discovery, made within a fully funded 25,000-metre program that has now logged 10,300 metres across multiple targets, establishes Sela Creek as a multi-zone district rather than a single-corridor asset — the structural upgrade that moves a junior from isolated-hole status to genuine discovery-scale consideration.

headline: LUCA DRILLS 4.7M AT 6.73 G/T AUEG IN NEW BRECCIA ZONE, BOARD LIFTS TAHUEHUETO BUDGET 40% (TSXV:LUCA)
source_name: Mexico Mining Center / Luca Mining Corp.
snippet: Luca Mining Corp. (TSXV: LUCA) announced July 7 that hole DDH26-246 at the Tahuehueto gold-silver mine in Durango, Mexico intercepted a new high-grade breccia zone returning 4.7m at 6.73 g/t AuEq including 0.6m at 14.80 g/t AuEq — a structurally different style of mineralisation from the known vein system, sitting immediately adjacent to current mine workings. Luca's board responded by approving a 40% increase to the 2026 exploration budget to $3.5 million total — a concrete signal that management views the breccia discovery as distinct and incremental, not incidental, to the existing Creston vein system.

headline: SELKIRK COPPER DRILLS 2.59% CUEQ OVER 4.5M AT MINTO YUKON — PEA IMMINENT AS PHASE 2 VALIDATES DEPOSIT
snippet: Selkirk Copper Mines announced July 8 initial Phase 2 results at the Minto copper-gold-silver project in Yukon, with hole 26SCM183 returning 2.59% CuEq over 4.5m within a broader 11.9m interval at 1.44% CuEq — confirming high-grade mineralisation at the former Capstone Mining open-pit operation, which was in production until 2023. The 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate and Preliminary Economic Assessment are on track for completion this month, making Minto one of the few Yukon copper projects where a development decision could be reached within 2026 — squarely in the window when supply deficits are expected to bite hardest.

headline: COPPER BREAKS BELOW $6/LB ON DOLLAR SURGE — MIDDLE EAST ESCALATION HAMMERS MANUFACTURING OUTLOOK, 2-WEEK LOW
snippet: Copper futures fell toward $6 per pound on July 8, hitting a two-week low as the confirmed US-Iran exchange drove the dollar sharply higher and raised fears of an oil-driven global growth slowdown — the inverse of copper's typical geopolitical response, where conflict usually lifts industrial metals rather than depressing them. The dollar-index break above 100 is the technical trigger: copper is dollar-denominated, and a sustained dollar breakout suppresses local-currency copper prices across major importing regions including China, cooling demand expectations at the margin even as the structural supply deficit remains intact.

headline: GOLDGROUP WINS BC COURT SIGN-OFF ON GOLD RESOURCE DEAL — $372M MEXICO GOLD MERGER CLOSES JULY 17 (NYSE:GORO)
snippet: Goldgroup Mining obtained final approval from the British Columbia Supreme Court on July 6 for its arrangement with Gold Resource Corporation (NYSE: GORO), clearing the last major hurdle for a $372 million business combination set to close July 17 — creating a Mexico-focused precious metals producer with four operating assets spanning the Cerro Prieto and San Francisco mines in Sonora, the Don David mine in Oaxaca, and the Back Forty project in Michigan. The 99.99% shareholder support at both companies' July 2 meetings and same-week court sign-off confirms a straight-line close; GORO holders will receive shares in a 4:1 consolidated Goldgroup structure targeting NYSE American uplisting.

headline: DE-DOLLARIZATION ALERT: 45% OF CENTRAL BANKS PLAN TO ADD GOLD, 74% SEE DOLLAR DECLINE — RESERVE SHIFT ACCELERATING
snippet: A Money Metals analysis published July 7 synthesises the World Gold Council's 2026 Central Bank Gold Reserves Survey — where a record 45% of central bank respondents plan to increase gold holdings in the next twelve months — with OMFIF data showing 74% of central bankers expect a moderate or significant decline in dollar holdings over the same period. The convergence of two independent institutional surveys pointing in the same direction strips the 'outlier' argument from either dataset: central banks are on a multi-year structural rotation out of dollar reserves into gold that will sustain baseline demand regardless of near-term hawkish Fed headwinds from the Hormuz oil shock.

headline: IS JULY 2026 LIBERATION MONTH FOR MONETARY METALS? GATA ARGUES GOLD AND SILVER SHOULD REFLECT DOLLAR'S TRUE VALUE
snippet: Writing for GoldSeek on July 5, the Gold Anti-Trust Action Committee's Chris Powell asks whether July 2026 — the US semiquincentennial — will be the month monetary metals finally reflect the true purchasing power of the currencies they're priced against, arguing that record sovereign debt levels, a Fed chair who withheld his dot-plot projection, and a dollar whose reserve status is eroding at a pace not seen since the 1970s all point toward an inevitable revaluation. The piece is more historical-framing than tactical, but GATA's track record of documenting institutional gold market dynamics gives it a readership that includes practitioners who influence the physical market.
